Qatar Real Estate Sector Hit by Major Ransomware Attack, Disrupting Operations

A significant ransomware attack targeting real estate firms across Qatar has forced the suspension of numerous property transactions and disrupted day-to-day operations for many agencies, industry sources confirmed on Tuesday.

The incident, first detected late Sunday evening, has affected the internal IT systems of several leading property management and brokerage companies, including Gulf Land Developments and Al Baraka Realty. Employees at these firms reported being locked out of critical digital platforms used for property listings, tenant management, and contract processing.

“Our teams are currently unable to access client databases or process new lease agreements,” said Salim Al-Mohannadi, Operations Director at Al Baraka Realty. “We are working closely with cybersecurity experts to assess the full extent of the breach and restore services as quickly as possible.”

Industry insiders say the attack has left hundreds of real estate agents and office staff unable to carry out their regular duties. Open houses and site viewings have been postponed, while property sales and rental registrations have slowed to a near halt. The Qatar Real Estate Association issued a statement urging member firms to temporarily suspend online transactions and review their cybersecurity protocols.

“Cyberattacks like this can paralyze the sector, especially as so much of our business now relies on digital platforms,” said Mariam Al-Farouqi, an independent real estate analyst based in Doha. “The immediate impact is a backlog in transactions and significant uncertainty for workers.”

The attack, which is still ongoing, is the first large-scale cybersecurity incident to hit Qatar’s real estate industry in recent years. While no data breaches have been confirmed yet, some firms have received ransom demands in cryptocurrency. Authorities are investigating the source of the attack.

Industry observers warn that full recovery may take days, with financial repercussions likely to emerge in the coming weeks.
